messages:
Jesse: FYI support escalated a customer 401/429 combo hitting /v1/generate. They also attached a pen-test report that shows an alias enumeration technique plus note about missing CloudTrail events. Need triage and retest plan.
Marta: Thanks — can we get the exact repro steps and the customer's request IDs? Also: which environment (prod/dedicated/private)?
Jesse: Customer on hosted prod. Request IDs: req_3a8f0b / req_3a8f1c. Minimal repro pasted below (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b","input":"hello"}'
```
Response alternates between 200, 401 with body `{"error":"invalid auth"}` and 403 when hitting different alias names.
Devin: That alternating 401/403 pattern smells like a KMS permission gap + fallback routing. If a model variant is backed by a different key alias and DescribeKey/Decrypt return different errors, it could leak alias existence. Kevin, does that match your pen findings? 
Kevin: Yes — my PoC uses timing and error content to infer available aliases. Short excerpt of responses: `{"error":"invalid auth"}` vs `{"error":"key not found"}`. I can reproduce with low-priv credentials. I attached the original test script in the report (redacted). Severity I flagged as HIGH because the alias enumeration allows targeted probing of key-backed models and could help chain to other behaviours.
Marta: Can you drop the repro steps inline here (just the curl + headers) so infra can run in staging? Also we need a minimal CloudTrail sample covering the times in Jesse's request IDs.
Jesse: Pasted the customer's redacted CloudTrail snippet: action: KMS:Decrypt failed attempts around 2024-05-12T14:03Z, but there are gaps where we expect DescribeKey events. I think CloudTrail was not capturing some KMS DescribeKey calls due to sampling config.
Priya: Tagging SRE & Compliance: we need to know retention window and if these events were archived. @Devin can you confirm CloudTrail config for the hosted cluster for that tenant (region us-west-2)?
Devin: Checking now — hosted global account has management events enabled, but data events for KMS are off by default. Retention is 90d for logs in s3, but indexing into our observability only keeps 30d. If the customer accessed older traces, they might be missing.
InfraBot: Created ticket SEC-4321: "alias-enumeration + missing-audit-events - customer escalations" (assigned to eng-security). Link: https://go/redwood/SEC-4321
Marta: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) Standardize KMS/error responses so error bodies don't differ by alias existence. 2) Harden KMS IAM: deny DescribeKey/KeyPolicy for unauthenticated or low-priv routes. 3) Enable/route KMS data events to observability for affected tenants. Thoughts? 
Kevin: Mitigation 1 is quick but partial. Standardizing errors prevents this leakage surface. But I still argue for tighter IAM and audit enablement. If not fixed, I keep HIGH severity.
Devin: For the IAM change: we can push a policy to deny kms:DescribeKey for token-scoped API keys immediately, but need a quick rollout plan (canary -> 100%). I also want to avoid breaking legitimate admin flows — will coordinate with Console team.
Jesse: Customer asked for ETA and proof of fix. Can we do a retest window? They prefer within 48h.
Marta: Plan: (A) Apply standardized error text in the serving runtime in staging today (small PR). (B) Turn on KMS data events + pipeline for the tenant (config change) — takes ~4hrs. (C) Apply deny-DescribeKey policy to token-scoped principals behind a feature flag, rollout canary to 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 24h. (D) Request pen tester @Kevin to retest after (A)+(B).
Kevin: I can retest after (A)+(B). My retest checklist: capture full HTTP traces, curl commands, and CloudTrail/KMS logs. Evidence needed: 1) before/after responses demonstrating error homogenization, 2) CloudTrail entries showing DescribeKey attempts (or lack thereof), 3) artifact demonstrating inability to enumerate aliases. Example test command I use: 
```
for alias in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOW_PRIV" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b","key_alias":"alias_test'"$alias"'"}' \
  | jq -r '.error' >> results.txt
done
```
Then diff results.txt pre/post.
Priya: Compliance ask: preserve the raw CloudTrail + KMS logs snapshot for the customer window and attach to SEC-4321. Also record decision tree and severity rationale for audit. I prefer severity moderated to MEDIUM until retest completes and we know exploitability in production.
Marta: I'll open a short PR for the runtime error normalization now. Devin, can you queue the KMS data event enablement and the IAM patch as an infra change? Tag me when canary is ready.
Devin: Will do. Scheduling: KMS events pipeline in ~3h, IAM policy rollout in ~8h (canary). I'll post deploy bot links here once queued.
InfraBot: Deployment queued: "runtime/error-normalize" -> canary 5% at 1719900600. Track: https://go/redwood/deploy/5678
Jesse: Customer notified: we planned mitigations and will retest within 48h. They acknowledged :thumbsup:.
Kevin: After I run retest I'll upload artifacts to SEC-4321 and add a verdict. If enumeration is still possible under low-priv keys, severity stays HIGH.
Marta: Agreement: mark issue as "in-progress". If retest fails, escalate to CISO and open customer incident notification. If retest passes, we'll close with follow-up tickets for audit retention and account-level hardening.
Priya: Noted — I'll prepare the compliance writeup template. Adding retention policy change to SEC-4321 subtasks. :white_check_mark:
Devin: Posting canary link when live.
Marta: Thanks all. Short status update to #incidents once retest finishes.
